# A C test's t.setContext writes the var the program holds the context in,
# `__ctx_<name>`, as Go's agent writes the Model's field: the build is passed
# the value already (passContext), but a handler reads the program's var
# when it runs, so a click after the setContext said "hello". win32 asks for
# stdlibContextParam as gtk4 does; without it a provider reached NoRef
# unlowered and the launcher panicked.

sngl test --platform=gtk4 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +3 tests, 0 failures'

sngl test --platform=win32 --language=c app.sngl
stdout 'ok +3 tests, 0 failures'
sngl test --platform=win32 --language=go app.sngl
stdout 'ok +3 tests, 0 failures'

-- app.sngl --
import test "sngl:test"
import ui "sngl:ui"

context[string] #greeting("hello")

component page ui.node {
    var said = ""
    ui.vbox {
        ui.text #shown(value=greeting)
        greeting("inner") {
            ui.text #inner(value=greeting)
        }
        ui.button #say(text="Say", @click { said = greeting })
    }
}

ui.window {
    page()
}

func testAHandlerReadsTheDefault(t test.Test, c page) {
    c.say.click()
    t.assert(c.said == "hello")
}

func testAHandlerReadsWhatTheTestSet(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.setContext(greeting, "hi")
    c.say.click()
    t.assert(c.said == "hi")
}

func testTheBuildReadsWhatTheTestSet(t test.Test, c page) {
    t.setContext(greeting, "hi")
    t.assert(c.shown.value == "hi")
    t.assert(c.inner.value == "inner")
}
